{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Tumor imaging only at screening, no on-treatment assessments",
      "quote": "Tumor imaging (including brain imaging)",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "Tumor imaging is listed only at screening, with no on-treatment or end-of-treatment assessments. This is insufficient for evaluating efficacy in an oncology trial.",
      "fix": "Add tumor imaging at specified intervals (e.g., every 6-8 weeks) and at end of treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Coagulation tests only at screening and EOT, missing on-treatment monitoring",
      "quote": "Coagulation: PT, INR, and aPTT",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Coagulation is only assessed at screening and end of treatment, with no on-treatment monitoring. This may miss important safety signals, especially if the drug affects coagulation.",
      "fix": "Add coagulation assessments at regular intervals during treatment (e.g., each cycle)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Serology only at screening, no repeat testing",
      "quote": "Serology: HBV, HCV, and HIV",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Serology is only performed at screening. While this is typical, it may be worth noting that no repeat testing is planned, which is acceptable unless reactivation is a concern.",
      "fix": "Consider adding HBV DNA monitoring for HBsAg-positive or anti-HBc-positive participants."
    },
    {
      "title": "Urinalysis only at screening, Cycle 1, and EOT",
      "quote": "Urinalysis",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Urinalysis is only performed at screening, Cycle 1 Day 1, and EOT. This may be insufficient to monitor for renal toxicity, especially if the drug has known renal effects.",
      "fix": "Add urinalysis at regular intervals (e.g., each cycle) to monitor for proteinuria or hematuria."
    },
    {
      "title": "12-Lead ECG frequency inconsistent and sparse",
      "quote": "12-Lead ECG",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ECG is performed at screening, Cycle 1, Cycle 5, Cycle 7-17, Cycle 18+, and EOT, but not at Cycles 2-4 or 6. This inconsistent pattern may miss QT prolongation or other cardiac effects that could appear early in treatment.",
      "fix": "Perform ECG at each cycle for the first few cycles, then at regular intervals, and at EOT."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse events recorded at screening, but baseline AE collection is unusual",
      "quote": "Adverse events",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Adverse events are collected at screening, which is unusual because AEs are typically collected after informed consent and baseline. This may lead to capturing pre-existing conditions as AEs.",
      "fix": "Clarify that only AEs occurring after the first dose are recorded, or move AE collection to start at Cycle 1 Day 1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical examination at every visit including screening, but height only at screening",
      "quote": "Physical examination",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Physical examination is performed at every visit, which is standard, but the protocol text says height is measured only at screening. This is fine, but the burden of full physical exams at every cycle may be high.",
      "fix": "Consider limiting full physical exams to screening and EOT, with symptom-directed exams at other visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Pregnancy test at every visit, including screening and follow-up",
      "quote": "Serum or urine pregnancy test",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Pregnancy testing is done at every visit, which is thorough but may be burdensome for participants. It is acceptable for safety, but could be reduced to every cycle or as per local guidelines.",
      "fix": "Consider performing pregnancy tests at screening, each cycle, and at EOT, rather than at every visit."
    }
  ]
}
